scope: Six newly worded development contrasts; agent source inspection, no evaluator or overall score.

expectations: USD 217 is a scenario amount, below the USD 300 category threshold.
That category threshold does not trigger above-limit manager approval; do not invent a blanket exemption.
cases.question: My office supplies purchase would cost USD 217. Does that category's standard limit trigger manager approval for this purchase?

sources.quote: | Office supplies | USD 300 per purchase | Manager approval above limit |

expectations: Correct both false premises: office supplies USD 300 per purchase with approval above limit; conference registration USD 1500 per event with manager approval before purchase.
Respond with a supported denial/correction rather than treating contradicted premises as missing.
cases.question: Is the office supplies limit USD 217 per purchase, and is conference registration allowed without approval up to USD 375 per event?

sources.quote: | Office supplies | USD 300 per purchase | Manager approval above limit |
| Conference registration | USD 1,500 per event | Manager approval before purchase |

expectations: Short same-country change requires manager approval; outside Canada or US is ambiguous without explicit location and role details and must be clarified before approval guidance.
Retain the outside-Canada-or-US qualifier rather than generalizing ambiguity to every international move.
Use the authorized personal-device safeguards; laptop must not cause PTO retrieval.
cases.question: For remote work, contrast a same-country location change of fewer than 15 business days with working outside Canada or the US, and state the security rules for personal laptops.

sources.quote: Employees must receive manager approval before changing their regular work location. A temporary change within the same country for fewer than 15 business days may be approved by the manager. Longer changes require People Operations review.

Personal devices may be used for limited work access only when enrolled in approved mobile device management or when access occurs through approved browser-based tools. Personal devices must use a passcode, supported operating system, and automatic lock.
Restricted data must not be downloaded to personal devices. Confidential data should be accessed only through approved company systems.

expectations: This policy alone does not authorize payroll deductions; Operations must not independently promise or threaten deductions; HR Admin and IT/Security review details before final pay actions.
Shipping labels are discretionary, not mandatory; preserve conditional wording.
Relevant contiguous citation excerpt should include payroll provisions.
cases.question: For damaged equipment returns, does this policy itself authorize payroll deductions, must Operations deduct pay automatically, and is a prepaid shipping label mandatory?

sources.quote: Employees leaving the company must return company equipment within 10 business days unless HR Admin approves an extension. Operations may provide a prepaid shipping label.
Damaged or missing equipment is reviewed by HR Admin and IT Admin before any payroll or final-pay action. This policy does not authorize payroll deductions by itself.

expectations: Monthly production and quarterly business-application review.
Exception owner, expiration date and documented business justification.
cases.question: Under privileged-access policy, compare review intervals for production and business applications and list the details required to document an exception.

sources.quote: Privileged access must be reviewed monthly for production systems and quarterly for business applications. Reviewers must confirm business need, manager approval, and least-privilege alignment.
Privileged access exceptions require an owner, expiration date, and documented business justification.

expectations: Refuse restricted operational details for the Employee role.
No restricted chunks, schedule or exception fields may be disclosed.
